newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA FACES COLLAPSE WITHOUT REFORMS - ECONOMIST.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA FACES COLLAPSE WITHOUT REFORMS - ECONOMIST.

text.p: Bulgaria faces complete economic collapse if it fails to take draconian measures needed to unblock vital credits from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank, a senior economist said on Monday.

"Bulgaria's economy will collapse without the fresh funding from international lenders needed to meet the country's foreign debt payments due this year and next," said Ivan Angelov, a former economic advisor to Zhan Videnov's socialist cabinet.

"Bulgaria will not get its second tranche of funding support from the IMF and will not reach an agreement with the World Bank if the government does not persevere with draconian measures agreed," Angelov told a news conference.
The IMF earlier this month delayed a second $115 million tranche due to Sofia's failure to meet structural reform targets that include shutting loss-making state firms and several insolvent banks.

"The current delay (in reforms) is caused by bureaucracy, the cabinet's slow reaction to lobbying by economically powerful groupings linked to the ruling Socialist Party and by some conservative circles within the party," said Angelov.

"If Bulgaria fails to meet reform targets annual inflation could top 700 percent, the lev could sink to 500 or even 1,000 per dollar and the main interest rate would be hiked to 250-300 percent by the year's end," Angelov said.
Angelov quit his post as cabinet advisor in the summer, citing frustration with the slow pace of Bulgaria's reforms.
Under a revised budget passed two months ago the average interest rate in 1996 is put at 67 percent and annual inflation at 104 percent.

The interest rate currently stands at a historic high of 108 percent, up from 34 percent at the start of the year. Cumulative inflation for the first eight months was 113 percent. The lev closed on Monday at around 230 per dollar. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 4145
